feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: SO-Arena: Benchmarking the Capability Spectrum and Reliability of System One Models
entry.summary:
SO-Arena is a new benchmark assessing System One models across 11 domains and 5 capability families, evaluating both capability spectrum and decision reliability.

Why it matters: High aggregate accuracy in System One models does not guarantee reliable outputs, necessitating separate metrics for capability and stability in deployment.

entry.title: BirdDreams: Joint Perspective and BEV Video Generation for a Plausible, Reactive Driving World Model
entry.summary:
BirdDreams is an autoregressive driving world model that uses joint attention across dual video diffusion transformers to simultaneously generate perspective and schematic bird's-eye-view (BEV) video streams from a single camera image.

Why it matters: By predicting surrounding scene layouts as part of the generated future, BirdDreams eliminates the need for privileged future trajectory inputs while improving geometric control and vehicle motion realism.

entry.title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation
entry.summary:
GSTAR is a spatial-group co-scaling framework for discrete autoregressive image generation that achieves up to 64x spatial compression using a quadratic group-size scaling rule and a semi-autoregressive decoder.

Why it matters: It proves that aggressive spatial compression in discrete autoregressive models can achieve low-latency image generation without sacrificing reconstruction or generation quality.

entry.title: Duo: A Reciprocal World Model for Full-Duplex Interaction
entry.summary:
Duo v1 introduces the Reciprocal World Model (RWM), a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives streaming audiovisual inputs and generates real-time responses using unified autoregressive reasoning and dual rollout distillation.

Why it matters: It establishes an end-to-end framework for full-duplex interactive systems that unify continuous multimodal perception, cognitive decision-making, and streaming content generation without relying on external control pipelines.

entry.title: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
entry.summary:
PhysLoop is a unified harness that uses LLMs to guide, select, and correct video generation models, creating physically consistent training data and enabling inference-time video repair.

Why it matters: It establishes a framework for video generation models to recursively self-improve their adherence to physical laws with minimal human intervention.

entry.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers evaluated decision models as actors, judges, and teachers, demonstrating that models performing poorly as actors can still effectively teach policies by evaluating post-episode trajectories.

Why it matters: Models do not need strong execution capabilities as actors to serve as effective teachers for reinforcement learning, as retrospective trajectory evaluation provides sufficient credit assignment.

entry.title: TTB: Test-time Baking for Efficient Rendering of Decoder-only View Synthesis Models
entry.summary:
Test-Time Baking (TTB) speeds up decoder-only Large View Synthesis Models by baking cross-view attention into lightweight MLPs and disentangling context tokens to align training and rendering modalities.

Why it matters: TTB enables real-time, high-fidelity novel-view rendering from large neural view synthesis models without requiring explicit 3D geometry reconstruction.

entry.title: Open Vision Banana: A Fully Open Recipe for Generative Visual Perception
entry.summary:
Open Vision Banana provides a fully open-source recipe converting 4B and 9B parameter image generators into multi-task perception models via conditional image editing, outperforming the original Vision Banana on zero-shot semantic segmentation.

Why it matters: It establishes a fully reproducible benchmark and open-source codebase showing that generative image models can be effectively adapted into competitive, multi-task visual perception engines.

entry.title: Ropedia Xperience 2: A Gold Standard for Scaling Physical AI Environments and Behaviors
entry.summary:
Ropedia Xperience 2 introduces 1,589 metric-scale 3D scans and 4,230 egocentric human motion recordings to standardize physical AI data collection across interactive environments and retargeted behaviors.

Why it matters: It establishes a unified framework for converting physical 3D scenes and human demonstrations into interactive simulation assets to study scaling laws for physical AI.

entry.title: WorldDraft: If Code Builds the World, Can Video Models Just Render It?
entry.summary:
WorldDraft introduces a benchmark of 432 paired test cases across 48 executable 4D world families to evaluate video models acting as generative renderers for programmatically built code environments.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized framework for using video models as neural renderers driven by code-based 4D simulations, identifying key failure modes in current multimodal architectures.

entry.title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
entry.summary:
Factored One-sided Adam-Moment (FOAM) is a lightweight SOAP optimizer variant that reduces memory and compute overhead by using input-only preconditioning and a factored Adam-moment estimator.

Why it matters: FOAM provides the convergence benefits of second-order optimization methods at a computational speed and memory footprint competitive with standard first-order optimizers.

entry.title: UniSpark: Exploring Hybrid Attention for Multimodal Understanding and Generation
entry.summary:
UniSpark-9B is a unified multimodal model that combines full attention with GatedDeltaNet linear attention in a Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts backbone for joint visual understanding and visual generation.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that combining full and linear attention enables a single unified architecture to efficiently handle both multimodal understanding and high-resolution generative tasks.

entry.title: FAME-QP: A GPU-Accelerated Quadratic-Programming Solver for Real-Time Model Predictive Control
entry.summary:
FAME-QP is a GPU-accelerated solver for dense linear MPC quadratic programs that uses constraint-dependent operator representations and fused CUDA graph kernels to reduce latency.

Why it matters: It achieves lower latency for dense quadratic programming in real-time model predictive control, enhancing high-speed robotic control performance.

entry.title: Precision on Demand: Escalating Weight Bits at Uncertain Decoding Steps in a Small Local Model
entry.summary:
A dynamic precision method for local LLMs decodes at 4-bit precision and selectively re-executes uncertain steps at 8-bit precision based on entropy or top-two margin thresholds.

Why it matters: It offers a mechanism to reduce memory bandwidth costs during local LLM inference by selectively allocating compute precision only to uncertain tokens.

entry.title: DeepStress: Stress-Testing Deep Search Agents
entry.summary:
DeepStress is a dynamic stress-testing framework that replaces retrieval modules with synthetic environments to evaluate search agent robustness against degraded evidence.

Why it matters: It exposes critical reliability vulnerabilities in search agents, showing they often rely on unverified parametric knowledge or trust compromised external evidence.

entry.title: Sketching Language Models for Context Attribution
entry.summary:
A novel sketching algorithm estimates all $n$ leave-one-out context attribution values using $O(\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon)}/\varepsilon)$ evaluation calls, matching a proven oracle lower bound under a stability assumption.

Why it matters: It enables computationally efficient estimation of prompt token importance without needing to perform full model re-evaluations for every omitted token.

entry.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
entry.summary:
A learned classical energy model named CRAM achieves top accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme and Maze-Unique benchmarks while training at least 1,000x faster and using up to 282x fewer inference FLOPs than looped models.

Why it matters: Energy-based models offer a vastly more computationally efficient and stable approach for learning constraint-based reasoning tasks compared to expensive looped neural networks.

entry.title: From Delegation to Coordination: Learning Efficient Multi-Agent Deep Research
entry.summary:
LEAD-RL improves multi-agent deep-research systems by introducing a joint training framework with contribution-aware credit assignment for main agents and subagents.

Why it matters: Contribution-aware credit assignment solves the issue of penalizing useful subagents or rewarding misleading reports, optimizing both research accuracy and execution efficiency in multi-agent workflows.

entry.title: The Value of Thinking: Learning When to Reason in Hybrid Decision Models
entry.summary:
A hybrid decision model introduces zero-or-T thinking, using a self-routing block to dynamically skip or execute full autoregressive reasoning based on the estimated value of thinking.

Why it matters: It enables large language models and agentic systems to significantly reduce inference latency and token costs by selectively bypassing compute-intensive autoregressive reasoning steps without sacrificing task accuracy.

entry.title: STEALTH: Steganographic Text Encoding Agnostic to Low-Level Tensor Hardware
entry.summary:
STEALTH is a provably secure linguistic steganography scheme that enables reliable message decoding across differing GPU architectures, floating-point precisions, quantizations, and model families.

Why it matters: It eliminates the fragile requirement for bit-exact hardware and software alignment between sender and receiver in linguistic steganography while increasing payload capacity per token.

entry.title: Look It Up: Multi-bit LLM Watermarking via Codebook Search
entry.summary:
A codebook-based LLM watermarking scheme embeds n-bit payloads into u-bit codewords via token logit biasing, enabling accurate multi-bit payload extraction from short texts using Hamming or Levenshtein distance matching.

Why it matters: It provides a practical method for attributing short-form LLM-generated texts to specific sources using multi-bit payload tracking.

entry.title: Scale-Induced Semantic Shift in Visual Prompt Injection Against VLMs and Web Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers identified Scale-Induced Semantic Shift (SISS), a vulnerability where downsampling images enables vision-language models to extract hidden visual prompt injection instructions that are unrecoverable at higher resolutions.

Why it matters: Standard image preprocessing pipelines (like resizing and compression) can unintentionally act as an attack vector by exposing hidden prompt injections to vision-language models and web agents.

entry.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
entry.summary:
Controlled empirical experiments show that multimodal language models require dedicated vision capacity, but do not need pretrained visual priors or pre-fusion encoder placement.

Why it matters: Architects can simplify multimodal model training pipelines and decrease inference latency by replacing separate pretrained vision encoders with jointly trained, early in-fusion vision modules.

entry.title: Negative-Only Policy Optimization for One-Sided Verifiable Rewards
entry.summary:
NOPO addresses one-sided verifiability in RLVR by treating verified positives as unlabeled and updating policies strictly through reference-relative suppression of verified negative samples.

Why it matters: It enables effective reinforcement learning optimization for complex reasoning tasks where evaluating errors is easy, but verifying absolute correctness is impossible or expensive.

entry.title: Joint Null-Space Projection for Data-Free Model Merging
entry.summary:
Joint Null-Space Projection (JNSP) is a closed-form, training-free model merging technique that projects each task's weight delta into the null-space of all other tasks' top right-singular input subspaces.

Why it matters: JNSP enables highly effective multi-task vision model aggregation entirely offline, outperforming data-free baselines without requiring access to evaluation datasets or compute-heavy optimization passes.

entry.title: One Table, Many Queries: Benchmarking Generalist Tabular Models Across Generation, Imputation, and Prediction
entry.summary:
The One Table Benchmark introduces an evaluation framework across 56 datasets to analyze trade-offs, objective interactions, and capabilities of generalist tabular models spanning generation, imputation, and prediction.

Why it matters: It establishes unified evaluation protocols and objective combinations necessary to build single tabular foundation models capable of handling generation, imputation, and prediction simultaneously.

entry.title: Embodied First Exam
entry.summary:
The Embodied First Exam is an agent-native benchmark containing 1,156 tasks across 35 suites and 47 robots to evaluate coding agents controlling physical hardware.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized benchmark demonstrating that current state-of-the-art coding agents fall significantly short of reliably controlling diverse robotic systems in realistic physical scenarios.

entry.title: MACaQ: Fast, Model Agnostic Calibrated Quantization for Low-Precision Weights and Activations
entry.summary:
MACaQ is a fast, model-agnostic W4A4 post-training quantization method using online block-Hadamard activation transforms and Flip-Refinement to quantize models like Llama-3-8B 11x faster than prior approaches.

Why it matters: It enables fast, memory-efficient low-precision quantization of large LLMs and diffusion models without cross-layer engineering or architecture-specific modifications.

entry.title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
entry.summary:
SteerDistill is a quantization-aware distillation method using closed-loop teacher steering to correct environment-divergent failure rollouts in quantized LLM agents.

Why it matters: It enables W4A16-quantized LLM agents to maintain near-BF16 task success rates and produce shorter execution trajectories with significantly reduced training compute.

entry.title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
GTAGym is an environment and framework leveraging GTA V to evaluate and train autonomous agents on AAA game tasks using automatic engine-state verification and procedural task generation for reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: GTAGym provides an automated, scalable infrastructure to benchmark multimodal LLMs and train RL agents on complex, high-dimensional AAA video game environments without relying on human annotations.

entry.title: Ensemble Routing for Prompt-Adaptive Cost-Aware LLM Inference
entry.summary:
PISA and PISA-E introduce prompt-adaptive LLM routing and ensembling that combine soft cluster memberships with model-specific capability predictors to dynamically trade off inference cost and quality without retraining.

Why it matters: It enables Web-based services to optimize LLM deployments by dynamically balancing response quality and compute costs per request without retraining routing models.

entry.title: Read Less, Solve More: Token-Efficient Sparse Reading of External Content for AI Agents
entry.summary:
SparseRead is a reusable reading control layer for AI agents that dynamically filters external content to reduce token usage and latency without modifying the underlying agent model.

Why it matters: SparseRead significantly lowers API costs and execution latency for web-facing AI agents without compromising task accuracy or requiring model retraining.

entry.title: PhyRubric: Rubric-Grounded Diagnostic Evaluation of Physical Commonsense in Text-to-Video Generation
entry.summary:
PhyRubric introduces a rubric-grounded framework that evaluates physical commonsense in text-to-video models by decomposing captions into timestamp-grounded semantic and physical item scores prior to video viewing.

Why it matters: It replaces vague overall video quality scores with fine-grained, interpretable diagnostic feedback to identify specific physical principle violations in text-to-video world simulators.

entry.title: Test-Time Scaling for Diffusion Language Models with Frequency-Aware Remasking
entry.summary:
A two-stage test-time scaling strategy for diffusion language models uses frequency-aware remasking to preferentially commit tokens whose predictions fluctuate, preventing early trajectory collapse on complex reasoning tasks.

Why it matters: It improves diffusion language model performance on complex reasoning and coding benchmarks by encouraging alternative trajectory exploration during iterative decoding.

entry.title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
entry.summary:
Evolving Infra is an agent-adaptive LLM serving framework that decouples compute allocation from KV cache management to dynamically optimize prefill-decode splits and cache retention for agent workloads.

Why it matters: It mitigates prefill-decode load imbalances and premature cache evictions, significantly improving serving latency and throughput for dynamic, multi-step agent workloads.

entry.title: LEASH: Stay Safe in Agentic Robotics
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced RoboRisk, a 105-task closed-loop safety benchmark, and LEASH, a safety harness that uses multi-stage decision gates to significantly reduce foundation model harm rates in agentic robotics.

Why it matters: It provides a comprehensive closed-loop benchmark and a model-agnostic safety framework to mitigate physical hazards and security vulnerabilities in foundation-model-driven robots.

entry.title: Blind Variation, Selective Retention: Improving Creative Idea Generation in AI Scientists
entry.summary:
The BVSR framework improves AI idea generation by restricting task information during initial proposal generation and using past empirical outcomes to filter candidates before evaluation.

Why it matters: Decoupling information availability between discovery stages enables AI scientists to generate more novel hypotheses without increasing empirical evaluation costs.

entry.title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
entry.summary:
EarthRecord is a new benchmark that evaluates multimodal agents on 238 land-change questions using raw, un-preprocessed four-decade satellite imagery across 56 sites to test true land-change analysis performance.

Why it matters: It exposes that current multimodal AI agents rely heavily on prior knowledge or surface-level pixel shifts rather than reliably grounded, real-world Earth observation data.

entry.title: Where Does Alignment Emerge and What Does It Mean? A Closer Look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis
entry.summary:
A re-evaluation of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis shows cross-modal alignment persists in newer language models given clean captions, with unimodal cross-modal alignment sometimes exceeding explicitly aligned vision-language models.

Why it matters: It clarifies the validity of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis by proving data quality drives representation convergence across modalities without requiring explicit vision-language pre-training.

entry.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
entry.summary:
TorchCurves is a PyTorch library that implements learnable, differentiable vector-valued parametric curves using B-spline and Legendre polynomial bases.

Why it matters: It enables PyTorch users to integrate smooth, differentiable parametric functional representations directly into deep learning architectures without writing custom C++/CUDA kernels.

entry.title: Breakdown of Autoregressive Multi-Step Reasoning Under Concentrated vs. Diffuse Attention Head Dropout
entry.summary:
Evaluations on GSM8K show that spatiotemporally concentrated attention head dropout severely degrades autoregressive LLM multi-step reasoning compared to budget-matched diffuse dropout.

Why it matters: These empirical benchmarks demonstrate that autoregressive reasoning chains are disproportionately vulnerable to localized structural disruptions rather than total noise volume, informing fault-tolerance design in transformer architectures.

entry.title: Can KV Cache Be Reused Across Model Updates? A DeepSeek-V4-Flash Case Study
entry.summary:
A case study on DeepSeek-V4-Flash demonstrates that direct KV cache reuse across model updates yields speedups but causes functional divergence, decoupling task performance from native model behavior.

Why it matters: Directly reusing pre-computed KV caches across updated model versions can significantly lower inference latency, but system designers must account for behavioral divergence and task-dependent fidelity loss.

entry.title: Margin-Guided Token Credit for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
entry.summary:
Margin-Credit Policy Optimization (MCPO) improves RL with verifiable rewards by weighting token credit based on model hesitation, measured via top-2 probability margins from existing forward passes without added computational overhead.

Why it matters: MCPO provides a zero-overhead token credit assignment mechanism that significantly boosts mathematical reasoning performance in LLMs trained with reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Understanding Mixture-of-Experts Language Models Beyond Expert Boundaries
entry.summary:
Researchers developed Routing-Aware Magnitude Profiling (RAMP) to discover that MoE domain specialization occurs at the neuron level rather than the expert level, enabling a fine-grained pruning method called RAMPr.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that MoE specialization is neuron-driven allows for more efficient cross-expert model pruning, significantly reducing GPU memory footprints and latency with minimal accuracy loss.

entry.title: REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding
entry.summary:
REAL is an exact, unbiased loss function for speculative decoding that directly optimizes real Expected Acceptance Length (EAL) using path weights and Rao-Blackwellization without architectural or inference modifications.

Why it matters: It provides a mathematically exact objective for training draft models that improves speculative decoding speedups without adding inference overhead or requiring architectural changes.

entry.title: SinkState: On-the-Fly SVD of Recurrent States for Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving
entry.summary:
SinkState accelerates hybrid LLM decoding by dynamically compressing recurrent states via on-the-fly local SVD, capitalizing on low-rank linear attention sinks to cut memory traffic.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces memory bandwidth bottlenecks during decoding, enabling faster and more memory-efficient serving of large hybrid LLMs without loss of accuracy.

entry.title: Bits or permutations? Spending a fixed inference budget on weight precision or on option-order averaging in small local language models
entry.summary:
A study on Qwen3 models shows that spending compute on option-order averaging outperforms using higher-precision weights only when base weights are quantized to at least 6 bits.

Why it matters: It provides a clear practical rule for optimizing local LLM inference under strict compute budgets: prioritize 6-bit quantization before allocating remaining resources to multi-pass option-order averaging.

entry.title: An Augmented Lagrangian Approach to Lifted Bellman Linear Programming
entry.summary:
AL-LBLP applies the augmented Lagrangian method of multipliers to Lifted Bellman Linear Programming, using dual ascent to learn constraint multipliers instead of relying on fixed penalty coefficients or target networks.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need for target networks and hyperparameter tuning of fixed penalty coefficients in LBLP, enabling stable scaling to large batch sizes and complex long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: BARS: Budget-Aware Sequential Sampling with Refusal for Majority Identification under Unknown Distributions
entry.summary:
BARS introduces a budget-aware sequential sampling method that certifies the top-two answer gap to enable early stopping, budgeted voting, or explicit refusal when accuracy cannot be guaranteed within budget limits.

Why it matters: BARS prevents large language models from returning low-confidence majority outputs by providing mathematically bounded early stopping or actionable refusals to save compute.

entry.title: Representational Atoms in Neural Networks
entry.summary:
Researchers formally defined fundamental representational units (FRUs) in neural networks, established fidelity and stability evaluation criteria, and proved threshold-activated sparse autoencoders (TSAEs) can reliably identify them.

Why it matters: This work provides a grounded framework to extract monosemantic features and map internal neural network mechanisms directly to human-interpretable concepts.

entry.title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
entry.summary:
Tree-Ising repairs language model reasoning loops by casting BF16 weight edits into sparse discrete QUBO/Ising problems, outperforming LLM-agent weight repairs while consuming zero tokens and fewer weight edits.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that discrete, training-free model edits can be solved deterministically and cheaply via Ising optimization, providing a more resource-efficient alternative to LLM-agent weight-space programming.

entry.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
entry.summary:
RoboScript introduces World In-Context Learning (WICL), enabling frozen foundation models to learn robot manipulation tasks from a single demonstration via simulation rehearsal and context updating without updating network weights.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that frozen foundation models can outperform specialized end-to-end trained policies in robotic manipulation by relying entirely on in-context memory built through simulated rehearsal.

entry.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
WikiTrace introduces an evidence-linked memory system for LLM agents that links concise lessons back to trajectory summaries and raw execution logs to mitigate memory-induced degradation.

Why it matters: By providing a mechanism for agents to ground and verify generated lessons against original execution logs, WikiTrace makes long-term agentic memory systems significantly more reliable.

entry.title: Few-Step Streaming Video Generation via Condition Shifting
entry.summary:
APEX extends streaming video generation to few-step sampling by using condition shifting to eliminate independent fake-score networks, reducing GPU memory and iteration time while improving instruction following and visual aesthetics.

Why it matters: By removing the separate fake-score network in streaming video distillation, APEX lowers training compute and memory overhead while maintaining high instruction adherence and visual quality over long 180-second video generations.

entry.title: dNaViT: Discrete Codes are General-Purpose Visual Representations
entry.summary:
dNaViT is a Discrete Native-resolution Vision Transformer that uses residual modulation and grouped product quantization to convert images into a compact, discrete visual vocabulary suitable for both vision understanding and image generation.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that a single compact discrete token vocabulary can unify visual understanding, generation, and editing within the same native autoregressive framework used by language models.

entry.title: MMDM: Measuring Massive Multitask Decision Making
entry.summary:
MMDM is a new benchmark featuring 5,448 questions across 16 categories designed to evaluate non-autoregressive System-1 decision models on complex, long-context, and constraint-heavy tasks.

Why it matters: It reveals critical limitations in current non-autoregressive decision models regarding joint reasoning, constraint satisfaction, and multi-select tasks in long-context environments.

entry.title: Infrathon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Real-World, Long-Horizon AI Infra Optimization
entry.summary:
Infrathon is a benchmark that evaluates frontier AI agents on long-horizon infrastructure optimization tasks over 24-hour evaluation budgets.

Why it matters: Short-horizon benchmarks misrepresent true model rankings and miss optimization gains that only emerge when agents run over extended timeframes.

entry.title: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance
entry.summary:
FINCOSMOS is an open-world evaluation paradigm for financial agents that tests Web data retrieval, strategy generation, and backtesting without reference answers using programmatic verification and veto checks.

Why it matters: It reveals that current LLM agents fail completely in realistic, open-world financial tasks due to silent errors like data leakage and unverified strategies, while proving memory-based feedback can remediate these failures.

entry.title: WaveGen: Truly End-to-End Waveform Generation via Internal Spectral Trajectory Learning
entry.summary:
WaveGen introduces Spectral Forcing, a diffusion-based framework that generates text-to-waveform audio end-to-end without external codecs, vocoders, duration predictors, or self-supervised text/audio embeddings.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that competitive text-to-speech models can be trained in a single stage from scratch without relying on complex, multi-module pipelines or pretrained external feature extractors.

entry.title: MotionGraphicsBench: Evaluating Motion Graphics Generation with Programmatic Verification
entry.summary:
MotionGraphicsBench is an expert-curated benchmark of 100 SVG animation instances evaluated using deterministic, human-readable verification programs instead of VLM judges or reference animation comparisons.

Why it matters: It isolates motion generation from graphic generation, offering an objective, code-based verification method that outperforms VLM judges for evaluating complex spatio-temporal LLM outputs.

entry.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
entry.summary:
ProTEUS is a mutation-resolved world model that combines a mutation-biased attention architecture with fast physics-constrained structural prediction for closed-loop, multi-objective protein evolution.

Why it matters: It enables rapid, computationally efficient traversal of complex protein fitness landscapes to design variants with significantly higher functional activity using minimal experimental rounds.

entry.title: PhysOPSD: Code as Privilege for Physically Plausible Video Generation
entry.summary:
PhysOPSD uses executable code from a simulation engine as privileged physical context within an On-Policy Self-Distillation framework to generate physically plausible videos.

Why it matters: It enables video generative models to adhere to physical laws and complex interactions using a lightweight dataset of programmatically controlled simulations.

entry.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training
entry.summary:
Deletion Tuning acquires new LLM capabilities by zeroing under 0.05% of pretrained weights via a binary mask on gate projections, matching full fine-tuning performance without altering unmasked weights.

Why it matters: This method drastically reduces post-training checkpoint sizes by hundreds to thousands of times compared to FFT while preserving base-model performance on prior tasks.

entry.title: e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)
entry.summary:
e-means optimizes mini-batch k-means using exponential moving average updates, matching or beating Lloyd's k-means loss in one-tenth the epochs.

Why it matters: e-means enables order-of-magnitude faster, scalable clustering for massive embedding datasets, drastically cutting GPU compute costs for quantization, retrieval, and data curation.

entry.title: ExRL: Sample-Efficient Online Adaptation of Long-Chunk Policies via Execution Length Control
entry.summary:
ExRL achieves sample-efficient online policy adaptation by shifting RL optimization from high-dimensional action chunk vectors to a lightweight adapter that predicts execution length per chunk.

Why it matters: It enables practical, real-world fine-tuning of pre-trained long-chunk robot policies using minimal physical interaction data.

entry.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
WikiTrace introduces an evidence-linked memory system that reduces LLM agent degradation by connecting concise lessons to trajectory summaries and raw execution logs for on-demand verification.

Why it matters: Linking distilled agent memories directly to verifiable execution traces prevents performance regression caused by faulty, ambiguous, or misapplied past lessons.

entry.title: A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets
entry.summary:
This paper identifies coverage collapse in REINFORCE-based methods like PPO and GRPO and proves that Approximate Policy Mirror Descent with periodic reference resets prevents it, establishing global convergence guarantees governed by base model coverage.

Why it matters: It provides theoretical proof that resetting KL reference models prevents optimization stalls, giving practitioners principled guidelines for designing sample-efficient post-training RL algorithms.

entry.title: Stagewise and interpretable emergence of inside-outside computation in Transformer-based language models
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that Transformers learn inside-outside parsing algorithms on context-free grammars in interpretable, analytically calculable stages, developing a distinct encoder-decoder depth structure during training.

Why it matters: Analytically mapping the stagewise training dynamics of parsing algorithms provides a theoretical foundation for understanding how modern LLMs resolve syntactic ambiguity.

entry.title: Beyond Passive Imitation: On-Policy Mid-Training Distillation for Language Models
entry.summary:
On-Policy Mid-Training Distillation (OPMD) replaces next-token prediction in continual pre-training by sampling student trajectories at anchor positions and optimizing them using dense token-level reverse-KL rewards from a frozen teacher.

Why it matters: It provides a model-aware alternative to passive domain adaptation that mitigates training-generation mismatch and prevents performance degradation during continual pre-training.

entry.title: POEM: Output-Relative Block-Sparse Attention for Long-Context Prefilling
entry.summary:
Target-free Entropy-guided Residual Modulation (TERM) is an inference-time defense that adaptively modulates an LLM's residual updates using prompt-calibrated attention entropy deviations to mitigate jailbreaks without predefined safety directions.

Why it matters: It improves jailbreak resistance while limiting over-refusal on benign requests and avoiding the need for static, pre-trained safety vectors.

entry.title: TERM: Target-Free Jailbreak Defense via Entropy-Guided Residual Modulation
entry.summary:
TERM is an inference-time LLM jailbreak defense that dynamically modulates residual updates using prompt-calibrated attention entropy deviations, eliminating the need for predefined safety target directions.

Why it matters: It provides a low-overhead, inference-time safeguard against jailbreaks while reducing over-refusal on benign requests without requiring manual target tuning or offline steering vector extraction.

entry.title: Precision on Demand: Escalating Weight Bits at Uncertain Decoding Steps in a Small Local Model
entry.summary:
A dynamic quantization strategy for Qwen3-0.6B on GSM8K decodes primarily using 4-bit weights and re-executes steps at 8-bit precision only when output entropy or top-two margin thresholds signal token uncertainty.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that selective, step-wise weight precision escalation based on output uncertainty can recover near-full-precision accuracy while reducing total memory bandwidth consumption during local LLM inference.

entry.title: Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
Blurring the Block Boundaries (B3) accelerates self-editing block Diffusion Language Models by up to 14.5% by dynamically refining adjacent token blocks in parallel within a shared forward pass.

Why it matters: B3 advances the Pareto frontier for inference latency in diffusion language models, making non-autoregressive generation faster without retraining or adding hyperparameter tuning overhead.

entry.title: Forward-Value Discretization: Faster Stochastic Diffusion Sampling Without High-Order Approximation
entry.summary:
Forward-value discretization introduces training-free lookahead prediction models (F-DDPM and F-DPMSolver) that improve stochastic diffusion sampling efficiency without requiring higher-order approximations.

Why it matters: It enables faster, higher-quality stochastic diffusion sampling without retraining or relying on complex high-order mathematical approximations.

entry.title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
entry.summary:
Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution (FGSE) introduces a framework that treats LLM agent memory updates as structured hypotheses, validating them via transfer, falsification, and regression probes before committing them to persistent state.

Why it matters: It prevents local episode successes from inserting unverified or unsafe knowledge into an agent's long-term memory, ensuring safer and more reliable self-improvement.

entry.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
entry.summary:
LingBot-Touch is a tactile foundation model that unifies heterogeneous sensor data into a plug-and-play representation to enhance general dexterous manipulation across diverse policy architectures.

Why it matters: It enables embodied AI models to scale tactile learning by leveraging cross-sensor data despite heterogeneous hardware physics.

entry.title: WorldFoundry: Towards Unified Infrastructure for World Intelligence
entry.summary:
WorldFoundry is an open-source infrastructure designed for reproducible inference and evaluation of generative world models across video, 3D/4D, embodied action, and interactive systems.

Why it matters: It enables unified, reproducible evaluation of persistent and controllable physical dynamics across highly heterogeneous visual and embodied AI systems.

entry.title: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence
entry.summary:
A2-MEAS is an embodied multi-agent framework that uses learned correction codes and the A2-WLA action model to improve robotic task performance and real-time failure recovery.

Why it matters: The framework significantly increases robot failure-recovery rates and task completion while operating at 4.03x the training throughput of existing baselines like pi0.5.

entry.title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
entry.summary:
Sage-Taiyi is a metacognitive AI architecture that uses explicit monitoring and control of scientific understanding to adapt research targets and select reusable reasoning methods for automated scientific discovery.

Why it matters: Demonstrates that metacognitive self-regulation enables AI systems to generate validated scientific ideations and directly improve real-world physical and chemical experiment yields.

entry.title: PCBRouteAgent: How Close Are LLM Agents to Becoming PCB Routing Engineers?
entry.summary:
PCBRouteAgent is a multimodal LLM agent that automates PCB routing by combining a Global Routing Planner with KiCad's native execution engine and bounded local recovery.

Why it matters: It demonstrates how LLM agents can orchestrate native EDA tools to bridge high-level strategy and low-level geometric routing in hardware design.

entry.title: Reframe: Observation-Aligned Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Visual Reasoning
entry.summary:
Reframe is a post-training framework for visual agents that aligns observation states using Ground-Drop-GRPO and Observation-Gated Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation without requiring a task-specific SFT cold start.

Why it matters: By aligning observation states and repairing faulty tool interactions mid-rollout, Reframe improves visual reasoning performance without needing task-specific supervised fine-tuning.

entry.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
entry.summary:
ReproBridge is an agent workflow that creates standardized reproducible ML artifacts to boost downstream coding agent reproduction success.

Why it matters: Preserving execution details and refined code enables diverse AI models to reproduce research experiments far more reliably and at a lower compute cost.

entry.title: Longtail-SWE: High-Quality SWE Tasks for Underrepresented Languages
entry.summary:
Longtail-SWE is a new benchmark featuring 202 repository-level issue-resolution tasks across 13 underrepresented programming languages, built using a solver-judge-repairer pipeline to fix defective tests and ambiguous task descriptions.

Why it matters: It expands software engineering agent evaluations beyond mainstream ecosystems like Python or JavaScript into 13 long-tail languages using higher-quality, repaired issue benchmarks.

entry.title: SIRIS: Can LLMs Tell When Simulation Errors Matter in AI-Driven Systems Research
entry.summary:
Siris is a novel benchmark that evaluates whether LLMs can determine if simulator errors and modeling limitations invalidate design recommendations in AI-driven systems research.

Why it matters: As LLM agents increasingly automate systems research using imperfect simulators, models must accurately discern when simulation inaccuracies truly impact real-world design decisions.

entry.title: How Much Training-Inference Mismatch Can On-Policy Distillation Tolerate?
entry.summary:
A study on on-policy distillation (OPD) demonstrates its resilience to training-inference mismatch from quantization and asynchronous rollouts, enabling faster FP8 training via a lightweight admission check.

Why it matters: The findings allow practitioners to aggressively optimize OPD training speed and memory efficiency using FP8 and asynchronous rollouts without sacrificing model performance or risking RL instability.

entry.title: InfraRSI: Harnessing Recursive Self-Improvement for Training Infrastructure
entry.summary:
InfraRSI is an agentic harness that applies a five-stage recursive self-improvement workflow to co-optimize LLM training launch settings, operator kernels, and communication schedules.

Why it matters: It enables automated, end-to-end optimization of distributed LLM training infrastructure while safely managing memory boundaries, hardware noise, and cross-GPU experience transfer.

entry.title: Steerable Multi-Objective Group-Relative Preference Optimization with Jointly Trained Low-Rank Adapters
entry.summary:
LambdaMix introduces a parameter-efficient method that jointly trains one low-rank adapter per objective using group-relative online reinforcement learning to enable real-time, preference-steerable policy selection from a single training run.

Why it matters: It enables language models to adapt dynamically to shifting user preference trade-offs at inference time using a single set of lightweight adapters, reducing both compute and storage costs.

entry.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
entry.summary:
CPU-ARC extracts robust, CPU-executable agentic reasoning caches from LLM reasoning traces, decoupling task-solving logic from model execution.

Why it matters: It enables low-cost, explainable, and energy-efficient deployment of complex reasoning workflows on standard CPUs without relying on expensive LLM inference for every task instance.

entry.title: Training Vision Transformers to Focus: Emergence of Spatial Attention Head Specialization
entry.summary:
A novel training method uses two visual focusing loss functions to induce spatial attention head specialization in self-supervised Vision Transformers without requiring annotations.

Why it matters: It improves the spatial precision and interpretability of self-supervised Vision Transformers, enhancing downstream dense prediction tasks like zero-shot segmentation without adding manual labeling overhead.

entry.title: FewStepRL: Fine-tuning Few-step Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
FewStepRL adapts RL objectives to few-step diffusion models via a three-phase framework comprising transformation, decomposition, and adaptation.

Why it matters: It removes the heavy computational bottleneck of rolling out many-step diffusion samplers during RL post-training while unifying diverse RL objectives into a single modular framework.

entry.title: Interpretability Is Not Model-Specific
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that interpretability tools like refusal vectors and sentiment probes can be transferred across different language models using linear maps fit purely on unlabeled prompts.

Why it matters: Interpretability tools like steering vectors and diagnostic probes can be reused across different AI models by fitting a map with a few unlabeled prompts, avoiding the expense of re-extracting them from scratch.

entry.title: DForkTree: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Fork-Aware Block Diffusion Draft Trees
entry.summary:
DForkTree is a training-free speculative decoding method that improves block diffusion draft tree accuracy by re-anchoring branches using local n-gram statistics and exact GPU tree construction.

Why it matters: It improves LLM inference speed over existing speculative decoding tree methods without requiring additional model training or architecture modifications.

entry.title: What the Loss Curve Misses: FP4 Pretraining Slows the Acquisition of Rare Facts
entry.summary:
Pretraining transformers with 4-bit floating-point (NVFP4) matrix multiplications requires up to 1.52x more exposures than BF16 to learn rare facts, despite showing minimal validation loss differences.

Why it matters: Evaluating low-precision quantization recipes solely on validation loss masks a significant drop in a model's efficiency at acquiring rare factual knowledge.

entry.title: A Geometric Invariant of Attention Predicts Head Specialization from Weights Alone
entry.summary:
Researchers derived a scalar invariant, ρ, that predicts transformer head specialization—such as induction heads—directly from weight matrices without executing forward passes.

Why it matters: It enables data-independent, zero-cost analysis and targeted context-extension fine-tuning of transformer heads directly from weight matrices.

entry.title: Lost in Rounding: bf16 Recurrent State Makes Hybrid Reasoning Models Think Longer
entry.summary:
Storing recurrent states in bfloat16 with round-to-nearest causes hybrid reasoning models to generate longer outputs and degrade accuracy, a issue resolved using stochastic rounding.

Why it matters: Serving hybrid reasoning models with standard bfloat16 RTN state caching severely degrades speed and accuracy, requiring stochastic rounding or explicit state-dtype reporting to ensure valid evaluations.

entry.title: Translating KV Caches Between Hybrid-Attention Language Models: MLA Latents, Linear-Attention States and Sparse-Attention Indexers
entry.summary:
Researchers developed methods to translate KV caches between hybrid-attention language models, enabling context hand-offs across MLA latents, linear-attention states, and sparse-attention indexers without re-reading prompt histories.

Why it matters: KV-cache translation drastically cuts latency and computational costs when handing off long-context conversations between non-identical, modern hybrid-attention models without requiring full prefill re-computation.

entry.title: When Answer Decodability Is Not a Decision: Separating Final-Answer and Imminent-Emission Signals in Chain-of-Thought
entry.summary:
Researchers developed Emission-Controlled Dual-Target Probing (ECDP) to prove that strong chain-of-thought answer decodability often reflects imminent token emission rather than an early, finalized model decision.

Why it matters: Probing high answer-candidate decodability in hidden states cannot automatically be interpreted as a finalized model decision without controlling for imminent text emission.

entry.title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
entry.summary:
HiVe-Mem introduces a multimodal memory framework combining graph-based horizontal expansion with trainable vertical evidence composition to improve memory retrieval and evidence selection for long-term agent interactions.

Why it matters: It enables multimodal agents to maintain broader long-term memory context while drastically reducing context-window token overhead through adaptive evidence selection.

entry.title: Shortcuts and Boundaries: Verifiable RL Misalignment and Contextual Safety Learning
entry.summary:
A framework encodes verifiable reward-context conflicts into task dynamics to study RL misalignment, showing minority shortcut exposure induces high violation rates while simple binary execution penalties improve capability and compliance across changing workflows.

Why it matters: Verifiable context checks allow scalable training of RL agents that maintain compliance and adapt safety behaviors even as execution rules and authorization levels evolve.

entry.title: MaxIM: Maximally Informative Incremental Summarization via Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
MaxIM introduces a capacity-constrained, information-theoretic reward-shaping framework for reinforcement learning that optimizes incremental summarization to maintain bounded memory over long-horizon interaction histories without human preference labels.

Why it matters: It enables LLMs to maintain accurate, bounded memory over unbounded context lengths for complex tasks without relying on expensive human annotations.
